informed_by.phase3a: Increasing related lexical surface multiplicity from K=1 to K=4 consistently moved the token-Markov-minus-trigram delta upward.
informed_by.phase3a2: Expanding coverage of arbitrary lexical codes from N=64 to N=1024 did not produce a monotone improvement, indicating that coverage alone is insufficient and motivating preservation of sublexical character structure.
informed_by.status: post-hoc exploratory follow-up, not a Level-2 retrofit

mechanism.base_form_invariant: Removing the final suffix glyph recovers the same encoded base form for every occurrence of the same plaintext token under a fixed key.
mechanism.name: base_form_suffix_variation
mechanism.suffix_choice: deterministic occurrence hash of seed, line index, and token index; plaintext token identity is not included
mechanism.suffix_set_policy: Fit one four-glyph master suffix ordering per source/seed. K=1,2,4 activate prefixes of the same master suffix order.
mechanism.token_length_control: Every ciphertext token is base length + 1 for K=1,2,4; K changes only suffix identity multiplicity, not token length.

primary_prediction: As K increases from 1 to 2 to 4, the exact-token Markov minus matched trigram validation delta should move upward toward zero or positive values, while the other four Voynich-direction relations remain positive. Because the complete monoencoded base is preserved, this mechanism is expected to retain more local glyph structure than the arbitrary lexical-code mechanisms tested in Phase 3A.2.
question: When every plaintext token preserves its full TRAIN-fitted monoalphabetic base form, does increasing occurrence-level suffix multiplicity from K=1 to K=2 to K=4 weaken exact-token sequential predictability toward the Voynich regime while retaining the strong local glyph structure needed by the other predictive relations?
